question: When the shopping trolley was first introduced in the 1930s, shoppers refused to use it. Men found it unmanly, and women said it looked like a pram. What did the inventor hire people to do in his stores to change their minds?
source_excerpt: Quick-thinking Goldman hired men and women of various ages to push the carts and pretend to be shopping in his stores.

extra.why_interesting: Today the trolley seems too obviously useful to need selling. Players don't expect that people once refused it, or that the fix was staged social proof, an early marketing trick they can work out from human nature.
extra.verification_notes: Sylvan Goldman hired men and women to push carts and pretend to shop to overcome the 'unmanly' and 'pram' objections; see https://www.405magazine.com/?p=22888

explanation: Sylvan Goldman paid models to wheel trolleys around his Oklahoma supermarkets, pretending to shop. Once people saw others using them, the trolley quickly became normal.
